title: SA/471/1995 of KUNWAR SINGH Vs SMT. NIRMALA DIVI AND OTHERS

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Second Appeal No. 133 of 2001
(Old No. 471-1995)
Kunwarpal Singh (since dead) ... Plaintiff/appellant.
Versus
Smt. Nirmala Devi and others. ... Respondents.
Mr. Jagdish S. Bisht, Advocate for the appellants.
None appears for the respondents.
Dated: September 27, 2012:
Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
 The respondents were served by way of publication.
Order was also passed by the Court about sufficient
service on 14.12.2011.
2. None appeared for the respondents.
3. Mr. Jagdish S. Bisht, Advocate is present for the
appellant.
4. Heard and perused the record.
5. Instant Second Appeal has been filed by the
appellants against the judgment and decree dated
24.01.1995 passed by Addl. District Judge, Roorkee in
Appeal No. 25 of 1993 'Smt. Nirmala Devi vs. Kunwarpal
Singh and others' arising out of Suit No. 16 of 1991
'Kunwar Pal Singh vs. Jai Indra Singh Verma and others.
6. The appeal was heard and was admitted on
12.01.1998, but while admitting the Second Appeal, no
substantial question of law was framed.
7. The Second Appeal is being heard on following
substantial question of law:-
"Whether the judgment of Lower Appellate
Court vitiates due to non compliance of the

2
mandate under Order XLI, Rule 31 of Code of
Civil Procedure?"
8. The facts in brief are that Kunwapal Singh, plaintiff/
appellant instituted Suit No. 16 of 1991 against Jai Indra
Singh Verma, predecessor-in-interest of the respondent
for the relief of specific performance of contract of
registered agreement for sale dated 22.09.1989 executed
by Jai Indra Singh Verma in favour of plaintiff on
payment of remaining sale consideration of ` 25,000/-
out of ` 45,000/- after adjusting ` 20,000/- paid as
earnest money before execution of the registered
agreement for sale. It was also prayed that the defendant
be directed to execute the sale deed in plaintiff's favour
and put the plaintiff in possession over the land in
dispute. Alternative prayer was also made that the
amount of ` 20,000/- alongwith the interest of ` 4,553/-
@ 17% per annum from 02.09.1989, the date of
agreement, totaling ` 24,553/- with interest during
pendente lite and future may be granted. In the plaint, the
plaintiff also pleaded that the defendant agreed to transfer
the land in question in plaintiff's favour for a sale
consideration of ` 45,000/- out of which ` 20,000/- was
paid by the plaintiff to the defendant as earnest money
and, thereafter, the agreement for sale dated 22.09.1989
was executed and registered; that according to the terms
of agreement, the defendant was liable to execute the sale
deed in plaintiff's favour upto 21.01.1990 after receiving
the balance amount of sale consideration; that the
plaintiff was always ready and willing to perform his part
of contract according to the terms of the agreement and to
get the sale deed executed, after paying the balance
amount of sale consideration of ` 25,000/- and the
expenses of execution and registration of the deed. It was

3
also pleaded that the plaintiff is still ready to perform his
part of the contract; the plaintiff requested the defendant
several times but the defendant evaded every time the
plaintiff's request. Thereafter, a registered notice
alongwith acknowledgment due was sent on behalf of
plaintiff to the defendant to remain present before the
Sub-Registrar, Roorkee to execute the sale deed, but the
Registered AD was not returned back to the plaintiff.
Therefore, the plaintiff sent another notice dated
05.01.1990 to the defendant to appear before Sub-Registrar on 22.01.1990, as 21.01.1990 happened to be
Sunday, to execute the sale deed, after receiving the
balance amount of sale consideration; that after the
service of the notice, the defendant sent a reply to the
plaintiff on 20.01.1990 to execute the sale deed in favour
of the plaintiff. The suit was contested by Jai Indra Singh
Verma by filing written statement, in which he denied the
plaint allegation. He pleaded that no contract for sale was
made by the defendant in favour of plaintiff. The
defendant has never executed any registered agreement
for sale in favour of the plaintiff to execute sale deed by
21.01.1990. He pleaded that some property in Abadi,
other than the land in dispute situate in village Kherajat,
Pargana Mangalaur, District Haridwar. He used to reside
in Delhi in connection with the business, therefore taking
advantage of defendant's absence, Brijbeer and others
were trying to take unauthorized possession over the said
property; that the relationship between the plaintiff and
defendant was cordial. Therefore, the plaintiff intimated
the fact to defendant. On receiving the said information,
the defendant came to the village on 21.09.1989. The
plaintiff advised him to file suit and obtain interim order
in respect of the said Abadi land in dispute. He decided to

4
file suit. As the defendant had not come with the expenses
from Delhi for suit, therefore he took a loan of ` 2,000/-
from the plaintiff and in that connection the plaintiff paid
the loan of ` 2,000/- to the defendant. Defendant signed
the document on 22.08.1990 and got it registered without
reading and hearing the contents thereof; that when the
defendant sent ` 2,000/- to the plaintiff, he returned the
same saying that when the defendant will come to
Roorkee, the cancellation of the debt security shall be
made and the payment of ` 2,000/- shall be received; that
the defendant was in no need at all to transfer the land in
dispute. Therefore, he was never agreed to transfer the
disputed land and execute the agreement for sale. In his
written statement, the defendant also submitted that the
agreement for sale is result of fraud played by the plaintiff
on the defendant, therefore, the question of transferring
the land in dispute for a sum of ` 45,000/- does not arise.
It was also pleaded that the allegation of the plaintiff that
he was ready and willing to perform his part of contract
was incorrect and notice was given with the sole intention
to create evidence for filling the suit. The defendant in his
written statement also submitted that he is ready to pay
back ` 2,000/- to the plaintiff.
9. The trial Court framed the following issues:-
1. Whether the defendant executed an
agreement to sale of the property mentioned
in the plaint with the plaintiff at a sum of `
45,000/- on 22.09.1989, after getting `
20,000/- as an earnest money and got
registered the agreement to sale?
2. Whether the plaintiff was always ready and
willing to perform his part of contract?
3. Whether the defendant took loan of `
2,000/- from the plaintiff, if so, its effect?
4. Whether the agreement to sale dated
22.09.1989 was executed by playing fraud?

5
5. Whether the defendant is entitled to take
benefit of Section 20 of Specific Relief Act?
6. Whether the valuation of the property
mentioned in the plaint was ` 2 lacs, if so, its
effect?
7. Whether the plaintiff is entitled to any
relief?
10. The trial Court decided all the issues in favour of the
plaintiff and decreed the suit and the defendant was
directed to execute sale deed in favour of plaintiff as per
the agreement within a period of one month. Aggrieved by
the said judgment, the defendant filed appeal before the
Lower Appellate Court bearing Civil Appeal No. 25 of
1993. The Addl. District Judge, Roorkee vide judgment
dated 24.01.1995 partly allowed the appeal and dismissed
the suit of the plaintiff for specific performance, however
the suit was decreed to the extent of ` 2,000/- to be paid
by the defendant to the plaintiff/appellant alongwith 17%
simple interest per annum from the date of agreement i.e.
22.09.1989. Aggrieved by the said judgment of Lower
Appellate Court, instant Second Appeal has been
preferred.
11. I have considered the argument advanced by the
counsel for the plaintiff/appellant and have carefully gone
through the record.
12. Learned counsel for the appellant referred the
judgment of learned Lower Appellate Court and pointed
out the findings recorded by the Lower Appellate Court at
different places holding that there is no force in the
argument of defendant that he was deceived. He also
referred that portion of the judgment in which learned
Lower Appellate Court held that defendant could not
prove fraud.

6
13. Learned Lower Appellate Court has given finding
against the defendant at different places, however allowed
the appeal of the defendant only on the ground that the
plaintiff could not prove the receiving given by the
defendant, as a receipt was given in lieu of ` 20,000/-
which was received by the appellant, but the plaintiff/
appellant failed to produce that receipt.
14. Order XLI Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure
provides that the judgment of Lower Appellate Court shall
be in writing and shall state:
(a) the points of determination,
(b) the decision thereon'
(c) the reasons for the decision and
(d) where the decree appealed from is reversed or
varied, the relief to which the appellant is
entitled.
15. In the present case, neither the points for
determination were framed, therefore the question of
giving reasons on such points does not arise. Entire
judgment is written in a form of story. While reversing the
judgment of trial Court it was the duty of the Lower
Appellate Court to discuss the issues decided by the trial
Court and to give its reasons for reversing the finding
given by the trial Court and also the reasons for its
decision. In the present case, this was not done. As
already discussed that no points for determination were
framed and discussed the judgment of Lower Appellate
Court vitiates due to non compliance of the mandate
under Order XLI, Rule 31 of Code of Civil Procedure. The
question is answered in affirmative.
16. Consequently, the appeal is allowed. The judgment
and decree dated 24.01.1995 passed by Addl. District

7
Judge, Roorkee in Civil Appeal No. 25 of 1993 'Smt.
Nirmala Devi vs. Kunwarpal Singh and others' is hereby
set-aside. The matter is remanded back to the Lower
Appellate Court for deciding the appeal afresh in
accordance with the mandate under Order XLI Rule 31
C.P.C.
17. No order as to costs.
18. Since the appeal is very old, the Lower Appellate
Court is directed to decide the appeal within a period of
six months from the date of producing certified copy of
this order.
